standard_prerequisites: Cartesian products, componentwise maps f sending a pair to the pair of component images.
The pair path construction: the inverse map from pairs of component paths to paths in the product, named pairpath by the author.
The action of a function on paths (ap) with its definitional behaviour on reflexivity.
Path induction and product induction with their conversion rules.
core_obligations: Prove that applying the componentwise map f to the pair path of p and q equals the pair path of the component actions of g and h on p and q.
Verify the well-typedness of both sides as paths in the image product, and settle the equation by staged inductions.
proof_roadmap: Check well-typedness: the left side is the action of f on a path in the source product; the right side is a pair path built from the component actions, which lands in the same path type since the projections of f are definitionally g of the first projection and h of the second.
By product induction, reduce the endpoints x and y to pairs (a, b) and (a-prime, b-prime), so that p and q live between the components.
By path induction, reduce p and q to reflexivity; under these reductions both sides of the equation become reflexivity of the pair, so the equation holds judgmentally.
Conclude the identification for all component paths.
difficulty_reason: A well-typedness check followed by a standard staged induction; each reduction is definitional.
